subject: StellarHealth order form — commercial & tax redlines
messages:
From: Susan Lambert <susan.lambert@stellarhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarhealth.com, legal@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: StellarHealth order form — pricing schedule & tax responsibility

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Procurement and legal reviewed the commercial exhibits and we have a few points we need clarified before we sign:

1) Pricing schedule: StellarHealth is asking for a clearer tier break on monthly committed tokens and an explicit ramp to accommodate our pilot month. Can you confirm which pricing band applies if actual usage in month 1 is 40% of the committed monthly volume?

2) Minimum commits & true-up: Your redline currently references an annual minimum commit expressed as a token aggregate; we need a monthly true-up mechanism and an illustrative example for accounting.

3) Net terms: Our finance team typically needs net45 on annual prepay exceptions. I see your standard is net30 — is there flexibility to move to net45 for this deal class?

4) Taxes & invoicing: We require clarity on withholding (if any), VAT treatment for EU usage, and whether Redwood will provide VAT invoices with line-level tax attributes. Also please confirm which entity will invoice and the country of tax residency for services.

We attached a procurement cover note with redlines from our team. Can we get a consolidated response and a single redlined order form that incorporates commercial concessions?

Sincerely,
Susan Lambert
Head of Procurement
StellarHealth

Attachments: Stellar_Procurement_Comments_v1.pdf (see inline comments)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lambert <susan.lambert@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StellarHealth order form — pricing schedule & tax responsibility

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate procurement/legal's thoroughness. Short answers up front, details and attachments below:

- Pricing band for month 1: We can treat the pilot month as a pro-rated band. If month 1 usage is 40% of the committed level, you will be billed the pro-rated amount (40% of the committed monthly charge) and that will count toward the annual aggregate. We'll add an explicit example in Exhibit A.

- Minimum commits & true-up: We agree to include a monthly true-up clause (example language in attached redline) with a 15-day invoice reconciliation window. True-ups are not automatic refunds — any shortfall will carry forward to the next invoice period unless otherwise agreed.

- Net terms: We can make an exception to net45 for this deal provided we move to a 1.5% annualized early payment discount if paid net30; however if Stellar insists on net45 we will accept for this enterprise pilot. Ben, can you confirm finance ok?

- Taxes & invoicing: Redwood will invoice from our US parent entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.) for hosted services. For EU VAT where reverse-charge applies, we'll include the VAT line and your VAT ID on the invoice. If withholding is required per local law, we will cooperate with standard gross-up language. We'll add an invoicing exhibit with line-level tax attributes in the redline.

Attached: Stellar_OrderForm_redline_v2.docx (redlines + tracked changes), pricing_schedule_v3.csv (banded tiers + sample pro-rating calc). Also linking HubSpot deal and DocuSign sign flow below.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm net45 concession (finance sign-off)
- Susan / Legal: confirm acceptance of invoicing entity and VAT handling
- Kimberly: I'll consolidate final redline after replies

Thanks — sending for quick turnaround so Legal can sign this week if possible.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Lambert <susan.lambert@stellarhealth.com>, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-18T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StellarHealth order form — pricing schedule & tax responsibility

Kimberly / Grace — quick finance check. Agree to the net45 concession for this customer class (strategic pilot) assuming:

- Deal_id HB-5892-Stellar is booked as enterprise pilot (SOW/PO present)
- We capture a billing contact with purchase order on the first invoice
- No other payment concessions (no extended credit plus discount)

If those conditions hold, finance will accept net45. Also confirming the monthly true-up with 15-day reconciliation window is operationally fine.

Grace, please flag any collections risk or VAT nuances I should be aware of — specifically if Stellar has EU entities we should map invoice routing to the correct legal entity to avoid double taxation.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Susan Lambert <susan.lambert@stellarhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@stellarhealth.com, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2027-06-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StellarHealth order form — pricing schedule & tax responsibility

Hi Kimberly / Ben — thanks for the quick answers and the updated attachments. Legal reviewed the redline and flagged two narrow changes:

• Tax residency line: Stellar requests that Redwood represents tax residency of the invoicing entity (US) and agrees to provide a VAT invoice where applicable. We need a short data point in the MSA that Redwood is the invoicing entity for hosted services.

• Invoice dispute window: legal asks that we move from 15-day reconciliation to 30-day dispute window for invoice disputes (procurement can still do a 15-day operational true-up but legal wants the formal dispute window to be 30 days).

Procurement confirms PO process: we'll attach a PO on the first invoice and acknowledge the net45 concession. On VAT: for any EU usage that triggers VAT, we'll share our VAT IDs and expect Redwood to include reverse-charge or VAT lines as appropriate.

If you can:
- Incorporate the tax residency sentence into Exhibit B
- Update dispute window language to 30 days (we're ok with the operational true-up staying at 15 days for reconciliation)

Once those two items are in the consolidated redline, StellarHealth legal is prepared to sign and route via DocuSign. Would you like us to counter-sign via our procurement portal or will you initiate DocuSign?

Thanks,
Susan Lambert
Head of Procurement
StellarHealth
